I would keep my full 20.8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is what fits my land, my irrigation conditions, and the way my family works. Since some people in my household work off-farm, I would not choose anything too labor-heavy or risky. I would use better seed rather than traditional seed, because I need stable yield more than I need to save a little money on seed. For wheat, I would put in enough fertilizer to support a solid stand and grain filling, and I would irrigate at the key stages because I have well water and wheat here responds well to that. I would use rotary tillage for wheat because it is practical for preparing the seedbed after maize. For maize, I would follow right after wheat harvest and keep the turnaround fast. I would use hybrid maize, put most of the nitrogen into maize because it needs strong growth in summer, and I would use no-tillage to save time and labor during the tight harvest-sowing window. I would spray only as much as needed to control the main weeds, insects, and disease risks, because I want to protect yield but also keep costs under control. Overall, I would aim for steady production, manageable labor, and low risk rather than pushing for the very highest possible yield.
